item.content:encoded: Milton High School and a Circle K convenience store in the area are operating under a boil water advisory, according to city officials. The advisory means water from those locations should be boiled before drinking or cooking until further notice. The city has not yet announced when the advisory is expected to be lifted. Residents and staff at the affected locations are urged to use bottled water or boiled water for drinking and food preparation until the advisory is rescinded. More details are expected as the situation develops.

item.content:encoded:
Tanger Outlets in Foley, Alabama is continuing a refresh of its property with the addition of two major national retailers. Victoria's Secret and Pandora jewelry are now open at the outlet mall, according to Tanger officials.

The openings are part of a broader effort by Tanger to enhance the shopping experience and modernize its Foley location. The company has been working to attract retailers that appeal to a wider range of shoppers.

Victoria's Secret will offer apparel and accessories, while Pandora will provide its signature charm jewelry and customizable collections. Both brands represent popular national retailers with strong customer bases across the Southeast.

item.content:encoded: Orange Beach is cracking down on e-bike and scooter safety with a new set of rules approved by the city council, according to WKRG News 5. The regulations aim to establish clearer guidelines for how riders can use bicycles, electric bikes, and other micromobility devices throughout the coastal Alabama community. The new rules cover safety requirements and operational standards for the increasingly popular transportation options. Details on specific regulations weren't immediately available, but the move reflects growing concerns nationwide about e-bike and scooter-related injuries and traffic safety. The rules could serve as a model for other Gulf Coast communities, including those in the Pensacola area, where e-bikes and rental scooters have become more common in recent years.

item.content:encoded:
Manna Food Pantries in Pensacola is hosting a unique community event that combines friendly competition with a serious mission: fighting food insecurity across the area.

According to event organizers, Pensacan 2026 invites teams to showcase their construction and problem-solving skills while directly supporting local families in need. The event structure allows participants to contribute their talents to a cause that addresses one of Pensacola's persistent challenges—ensuring adequate nutrition for vulnerable residents.

Manna Food Pantries serves as a crucial resource for food-insecure families throughout Escambia County, distributing groceries and essential items to those struggling to make ends meet. The organization regularly connects residents with emergency food assistance and longer-term support resources.

Teams interested in participating can learn more about event details, registration, and how their involvement will support Manna's ongoing work in the community. The competition format encourages both corporate and volunteer groups to get involved while making a tangible difference for neighbors facing food hardship.

item.content:encoded:
The Mississippi Highway Patrol is increasing patrols across the state ahead of the Labor Day holiday weekend, warning drivers to exercise extra caution on roadways, according to a news release from MHP.

Troopers will be on heightened alert beginning Friday as holiday travel reaches peak levels. The department is urging motorists to drive responsibly during the extended weekend, when roads typically see heavier-than-normal traffic.

While this enforcement activity occurs in Mississippi, drivers in the Florida Panhandle heading north for the holiday should expect similar increased patrol presence on interstate corridors that connect our region to neighboring states. Safe driving practices—including maintaining speed limits, avoiding distracted driving, and staying alert—remain essential year-round but especially during high-traffic periods.

item.title: Man Sentenced For Failing To Report Danika Troy's Body
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A Pace man has been sentenced to four years in prison for failing to report finding fourteen-year-old Danika Troy's charred body last December. Mitchell Eddins pleaded guilty to failure to report a dead body and stealing Troy's scooter, waiting nearly twelve hours before contacting authorities. Troy was allegedly…
item.content:encoded: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- A Pace man has been sentenced to four years in prison for failing to report finding fourteen-year-old Danika Troy's charred body last December. Mitchell Eddins pleaded guilty to failure to report a dead body and stealing Troy's scooter, waiting nearly twelve hours before contacting authorities. Troy was allegedly lured into the woods and fatally shot by two teenagers, Gabriel Williams and Kimahri Blevins, who then set her body on fire. Both teens face life in prison on premeditated murder charges, with upcoming court dates in September and November.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- With crowds heading to Florida beaches this holiday weekend, state wildlife officials are asking people to give nesting sea turtles and shorebirds plenty of space. F-W-C says staying at least fifty feet away, avoiding flashlights and flash photography at night, and filling in beach holes can all help protect hatchlings trying to reach the water. Officials also remind beachgoers to keep dogs leashed and clear away trash and gear before leaving the beach. Anyone spotting a distressed sea turtle is asked to call the F-W-C Wildlife Alert Hotline.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County celebrated the reopening of Perdido Kids Park this week with a ribbon cutting event. Commissioner Mike Kohler says the upgrades include new durable playground equipment, A-D-A accessible amenities, and new fencing, while keeping original features like the children's handprint wall and airplane rocker toys. The park, located on Gulf Beach Highway, is open daily from sunrise to sunset.

item.title: Scattered Storms Could Disrupt Labor Day Weekend in NW Florida
item.dc:creator: newsroom

According to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia, the activity should develop mainly after 1 p.m., with a 60% chance of precipitation…
item.content:encoded: A round of scattered showers and thunderstorms is expected to move into the Escambia County area Friday, potentially affecting holiday weekend plans for residents heading into Labor Day. According to the National Weather Service forecast for North Escambia, the activity should develop mainly after 1 p.m., with a 60% chance of precipitation throughout the afternoon and evening. Most areas can expect rainfall between a tenth and quarter of an inch, though stronger storms could produce heavier downpours in isolated spots. Temperatures will reach near 89 degrees with light east winds around 5 mph. Those planning outdoor activities for the holiday weekend should monitor conditions Friday afternoon and have indoor backup plans ready, particularly for late-afternoon gatherings.

item.content:encoded:
The unbeaten Tate Aggies volleyball team gave Florida's top-ranked Class 5A program all it could handle Thursday night, but ultimately fell 3-1 to the visiting Gulf Breeze Dolphins in a competitive district matchup in Cantonment.

Tate entered the contest with a perfect 7-0 record and faced off against Gulf Breeze, ranked No. 1 in the state and sporting a 9-1 record heading into the showdown. The Aggies stayed competitive throughout the wire-to-wire battle, showing they belong among the region's elite volleyball programs despite the loss.

The result marks Tate's first blemish of the season, but the performance demonstrated the program's strength in Northwest Florida high school volleyball.

item.content:encoded:
School administrators in George County, Mississippi have launched an investigation after discovering someone created a fraudulent social media account impersonating one of their teachers, according to WKRG News 5.

The fake page was brought to the attention of George County School District officials, who confirmed the account does not belong to the actual educator. While details remain limited, the discovery has prompted district leadership to look into who created the impostor account and for what purpose.

The incident highlights growing concerns about social media fraud and identity theft targeting educators. School districts across the country have dealt with similar cases where unauthorized accounts have been created in teachers' names, sometimes used to spread misinformation or harass school staff.

George County School District has not released additional information about the investigation or whether any disciplinary action will result from the discovery.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola State College celebrated the opening of its brand-new Pirate Soccer Field this afternoon. The field was inaugurated with a ribbon-cutting ceremony. Once the facility is more seasoned, it could also host soccer clubs and tournaments. Another project the college is working on is the beginning of a women’s soccer program for its charter high school, with hopes of eventually adding men’s soccer. The first game on the new field is set for 5:00p tonight against Northeast Mississippi Community College.
